messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary cluster 'canary-us-east-1' p99 latency spike detected at 6654321000. p99 = 2.8s (baseline 0.6s), p95 = 1.2s. Streaming stall rate increased ~3.5x. Auto-pager sent to oncall.

sarah: Oncall sarah here, I'm seeing the same in grafana. Streaming sessions show long stalls at the mux layer, many sessions stuck in 'waiting-for-kv' state. Any immediate blockers? :eyes: 

ajay: I'm looking at the rollout controller logs. Can you confirm current canary weight? I see a weight change around 6654319000.

incident-bot: Deployment event: rollout-controller applied traffic_shift for model:gen v3 -> weight 40% at 6654319052 (intended 2%). Source: automated rollout retry due to transient autoscaler behavior. Attached: /deploy/logs/6654319052.

morgan: Whoa 40% is huge. That would explain the unexpected load. Suggest immediate rollback to v2 and reduce canary weight to 0 while we triage.

sarah: Initiating immediate mitigation: executing rollback and hard-route to stable.

deploy-bot: Executing command: `redwood rollout set-weight model:gen v2 100%`

deploy-bot: Response: success. Traffic now at v2=100%, v3=0%. Rolling back canary.

ajay: Confirming metrics stream — p99 downtrend starting within 30s of rollback, but we still have tail stalls for long-lived streaming sessions that started earlier. I'm seeing KV cache miss rate spiking and evictions.

ajay: metric query (promql):
```
sum(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (pool)
```
Result: evictions up ~5x in canary pool; kv hit ratio down from 98% -> 82% for v3 worker set.

tilly: If KV footprint increased (tokenizer/chunking changes in v3) the warmup for existing hosts could thrash. We can temporarily disable multiplexing for the streaming path on the affected hosts which previously helped tail latency. Can someone flip mux=false for canary pool?

sarah: Toggling mux flag for canary pool now: `/infra feature-flag set streaming.mux false --scope canary-us-east-1`

incident-bot: Feature flag change recorded at 6654321120.

sarah: Observing partial recovery: p95 -> 0.9s, p99 trending toward 1.1s. Streaming stalls count down but ~8 long sessions remain stuck and need manual session reset.

raj: CS note: we've identified ~12 customer sessions impacted (long-lived interactive streams). Notifying CS leads and safety net. Impact: slow responses, some UI retries. No customer data loss reported.

morgan: Root cause hypothesis: rollout controller retry + autoscaler race caused unintended large canary weight. Model v3 changes increased KV working set (tokenizer + longer context caching) which amplified eviction/backpressure and triggered streaming stalls under multiplexed workloads.

ajay: Next steps I'm owning: capture heap/kv profiles for v3 hosts, save grafana snapshots and traces, collect tail traces for stuck sessions, and open postmortem. Creating internal incident ticket now.

ajay: Creating ticket: INC-2026-842 - "Canary rapid traffic shift -> KV eviction -> streaming tail stalls". Adding logs and snapshots: https://grafana.local/d/xxxxx/canary-6654321000 and link to traces.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to SEV2. Status page not required. Support ticket created: INC-2026-842. Pager duty: sarah -> ajay handoff.

sarah: Handing off to ajay for deeper mitigation and postmortem. Handoff timestamp: 6654321350. @ajay you'll lead the writeup and RCA. Thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:

ajay: ack, taking over. I will coordinate with eng-runtime and infra to gate future rollout-controller retries behind weight validation and add an autoscaler-rollout mutex. Will also propose a temporary canary weight ceiling.

morgan: Adding action item: enforce canary max weight 5% in controller config and add runbook step to flip mux if KV eviction > X.

raj: Notifying affected account leads and sending short summary. Will follow up with customer impact report after RCA.

sarah: off-call now. Handoff complete. Good job team. :tada:

(autosave: dash snapshots, traces, and logs archived to /incidents/INC-2026-842/attachments/)
